references.text: Proverbs 29:25 speaks of the fear of man as a trap, but whoever trusts in the Lord will be secure. This can be seen in connection with Matthew 13:12 about having and receiving more, versus not having and losing even what little one has, reflecting spiritual wealth and security in God compared to fear and loss.

Luke 8:18 is about being attentive to how one hears; for whoever has will receive more, but whoever does not have will lose even what they think they have. This directly mirrors the principle in Matthew 13:12 of having and receiving more versus not having and losing.

Matthew 25:29 concerns the parable of the talents, where it is said that to whoever has, more will be given, and they will have abundance, but from whoever does not have, even what they have will be taken. This is a direct parallel to the principle expressed in Matthew 13:12.

Mark 4:25 contains a similar statement as in Matthew 13:12, that whoever has will receive more, but from whoever does not have, even what they have will be taken. This points to the same principle of spiritual wealth and loss.
